rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for an explanation of al-Ṣamad given earlier, but this extract does not restate its content.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الصمد إلى آخر ما مضى عنه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and others explain al-Ṣamad as having no hollow interior and al-Aḥad as having no counterpart.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه وغيره : هو الذي لا جوف له , والأحد الذي لا نظير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣamad entails every perfection and freedom from defects; al-Aḥad entails that God has no equal.
rows.anchor: فاسمه الصمد يتضمن اتصافه بصفات الكمال ونفي النقائص عنه , واسمه الأحد يتضمن أنه لا مثل له

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines al-Ṣamad as the one to whom needs are directed, who fulfills them without needing another; thus God is Lord, never subordinate.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : الصمد - يعني بالسكون : - التوجه بالحاجات إلى ملي بقضائها لا يحتاد إلى سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second interpretation, al-Ṣamad is a negative attribute: it denies the quiddity and composition that entail need, affirming God's necessary existence alone.
rows.anchor: وعلى التفسير الثاني : هو من النعوت السلبية , فهو دال على نفي الماهية التي نعنت بها فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two interpretations together encompass prior explanations and every perfection and majestic attribute that can be affirmed of God.
rows.anchor: وهذان التفسيران الأول والثاني جامعان لجميع ما فسر به ولما عسى أن يقال فيه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all beings need God absolutely while He needs none, He alone deserves worship, creates benefit and harm, and can preserve what He wills.
rows.anchor: وأنه هو وحده المستحق للعبادة لاحتياج الكل إليه الاحتياج المطلق وغناه عنهم الغنى المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣamad refutes rival cosmic-governance claims, including Sabians who assign governance to the stars and anyone who assigns it to other than God.
rows.anchor: والصابية القائلين بتدبير النجوم , وعلى غيرهم من كل من ادعى تدبيرا لغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God's complete self-sufficiency and governance produces total entrusting and reliance, which is lordship's oneness.
rows.anchor: أنتج له كمال التفويض والتوكل وهو توحيد الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four names indicate spiritual stations: the intimate see all else as contingent, the people of the right turn to Allah, and the people of the left need reminders of unity; this rebukes unionists.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأسماء الأربعة مشيرة إلى مقامات السائرين ومرامات الحائرين والجائرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the view that God is this divided, dependent world.
rows.anchor: إن الإله هو هذا العالم , وهو منقسم بالحسن فضلا عما عداه ومحتاج أشد احتياج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wholly uncomposed, sustains all things, and gives existence generously to every existent without sharing a genus or likeness with anything.
rows.anchor: وأنه المعطي لوجود جميع الموجودات , والمفيض للجود على كل الماهيات فلا يجانس شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having offspring cannot complete God's power or lordship: generation entails need, and divine power does not apply to impossibilities; al-Ṣamad makes it impossible.
rows.anchor: وهذا محال , لأنه سبحانه صمد , فكان ذاك بيانا للصمدية في كلا معنييها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam yalid denies any generation from God, since offspring entails an interior and need, whereas He eternally needs no successor or helper; this rejects claims about angels, Ezra, or Christ as offspring.
rows.anchor: فهو رد على من قال : الملائكة بنات الله أو عزير أو المسيح أو غيره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam yulad establishes that God has no genus and no beginning: birth requires matter, and anything connected to matter is generated from another.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو تولد عنه غيره تولد هو عن غيره كما هو المعهود والمعقول , فهو قديم لا أول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God's identity is self-subsistent and existence alone, being generated would negate His identity, oneness, and self-sufficiency; therefore nothing can be generated from or equal to Him.
rows.anchor: ومن كانت هويته لذاته لم يصح بوجه أن يتولد عن غيره لأنه لو تولد عن غيره لم يكن هو هو لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses lam yakun as never coming to exist in any way, lahu as exclusively His, kufuwan as an equal, and aḥad as anyone at all.
rows.anchor: { ولم يكن } أي لم يتحقق ولم يوجد بوجه من الوجوه ولا بتقدير من التقادير { له } أي خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one equals God in necessary existence: such equality would require genus and differentiating species, a derivation by pairing that the preceding verses exclude.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو ساواه في ذلك لكانت مساواته باعتبار الجنس والفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once no equal shares His existence, no one can equal the power of His acts; the three clauses jointly explain al-Ṣamad and form one statement.
rows.anchor: فعطف هاتين الجملتين على الجملة التي قبلها لأن الثلاث شرح الصمدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase lahu is fronted to emphasize that the greatest concern is denying an equal to God's essence; kufuwan is circumstantial of aḥad.
rows.anchor: وقدم الظرف في الثالثة لأن المقصود الأعظم نفي المكافأة عن الذات الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parsing treats kana as incomplete and kufuwan as its predicate, licensed by its restriction through lahu, as in the cited Quranic construction.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( كان ) ناقصة ويكون ( كفوا ) خبرها , وسوغ خبريته تخصيصه ب ( له )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah proceeds from pure identity to divinity, oneness, and self-sufficiency, then denies generation and every equal because God has no genus or species.
rows.anchor: فمن أول السورة إلى آخر الأسماء في بيان حقيقته سبحانه وتعالى ولوازمها الأقرب فالأقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observed events, especially the Prophet's victory over abundant hostile forces as he foretold, demonstrate that no one equals God's power of action.
rows.anchor: بدلالة شاهد الوجود الذي كشف عنه والشهود بنصر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unattributed poetic lines emphasize that divine majesty exceeds both human reach and the strongest speaker's description.
rows.anchor: : ( وأين الثريا من يد المتناول ) ( الأمر أعظم من مقالة قائل ) وبين المعنيين كليهما

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Ubayy ibn Kab that polytheists asked Muhammad to describe his Lord, so this surah was revealed; all born die and are inherited, but God neither dies nor is inherited, and none equals Him.
rows.anchor: وروى الترمذي عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله تعالى عنه أن المشركين قالوا : يا محد انسب لنا ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah gathers the beautiful names and highest attributes by purifying God from any consort, like, or equal, and rejects every contrary doctrine.
rows.anchor: وعلم أن حاصلها تنزيه المعبود عن أن يكون له مجانس , أو يكون له مكافئ , والرد على كل من يخالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran answers this surah in its ending-to-opening structure and refutes those who deify Christ or claim God begot him; Jesus is God's servant, created as He willed.
rows.anchor: لا سيما من ادعى أن عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام إله أو أنه ولد له سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brief as it is, the surah addresses divine essence and rebuts heresy; it is likened to a third of the Quran and to the belief that heads religion, whose other parts are speech and action.
rows.anchor: وكانت معادلة لثلث القرآن وهي ثلث أيضا باعتبار آخر وهو أن الدين اعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's sequence signals God's identity through the pronoun, His name, oneness, self-sufficiency, the denial of generation, and finally the denial of any equal, evidenced by His acts.
rows.anchor: دل على الذات الأقدس بالهوية , وعبر عنها بالضمير إشارة إلى نفي الماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's relentless public denunciation made the Prophet's message famous; when its truth was established, that notoriety turned into an even greater renown for truth and victory.
rows.anchor: فكانت تلك الشهرة عين الرفة والنصرة , لأن الشيء , إذا خرج عن حده انقلب غلى ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversal of public opposition is extraordinary evidence that the lone Prophet spoke truth while innumerable opponents lied, and that God is mighty and wise in how He brought it about.
rows.anchor: فدل هذا الفعل الأعظم من صدق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو وحده , وكذب المعاندين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This observed victory establishes that God has no equal and hence cannot beget or be begotten; it refutes the divinity of Christ and all claims of divine offspring.
rows.anchor: فعلم قطعا أنه لا كفوء له , فعلم أنه لا يصح أصلاص أن يلد ولا أن يولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage unfolds ten implications: eternal necessary existence; freedom from defect; every perfection; transcendence beyond body, substance, indwelling, or union; and absolute independence from creator, father, or benefactor.
rows.anchor: الأول أنه تعالى له الوجود الذي ما مثله فليس هو كالممكنات المسبوقة بالعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its remaining implications are absolute oneness, uniqueness in ownership and governance, majesty lacking no perfection, and might without opponent or equal; the ten map onto the surah.
rows.anchor: السابع أنه تعالى له الوحدانية التي ليس فيها شبيه أي في صفاته , ولا مثيل أي في نوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with the pronoun after the preceding account of victory signifies that one who purifies the inward through God's name receives victory; the close of al-Baqara expresses the same divine oneness and sustaining power.
rows.anchor: وابتدأ سبحانه السورة بالضمير قبل الظاهر بعد التصريح بالنصر والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is present in every age and heart, while all else is essentially absent and dependent; He alone is ungenerated, self-sufficient, all-encompassing, and beyond direct comprehension except through attributes and effects.
rows.anchor: وهو هو الذي هو - مع كونه غيب الغيب - مستحضر في كل لب , لا يظهر بغيب عن أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is both praised for perfection and sanctified beyond defect; glorification implies sanctification and sanctification implies glorification, together affirming uniqueness while denying likeness.
rows.anchor: التقديس مضمر في صريح التسبيح , والتسبيح مضمر في صريح التقديس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-Ṣamad combines affirmation and negation: its lordly sense affirms perfect attributes, while having no interior negates limit, direction, body, substance, and composition.
rows.anchor: فهو جامع بين الأمرين فإنه جمع كل صفة لا يتم الخلق إلا بها

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says people asked the Prophet about good while he asked about evil, since knowing evil helps one avoid falling into it.
rows.anchor: حتى قال حذيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه ( وكان الناس سألون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الخير , وكنت أسأله عن الشر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testimony of faith begins with negation because newcomers must clear falsehood before receiving truth; this surah starts with affirmation for perfected believers and ends by negating all rivals.
rows.anchor: فلما نفت أولا كل غير كان سببا للمجانبة والبعد عن حضرات القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣamad's linguistic sense is the master to whom needs return, affirming the attributes needed for the order of all actions.
rows.anchor: ( لأن أحد مدلوليه ) في اللغة : السيد الذي يرجع إليه , فاقتضى ذلك إثبات صفات الكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second sense of al-Ṣamad, having no interior, excludes an end, limit, direction, body, or substance.
rows.anchor: لأن ثاني مدلوليه في اللغة : الذي لا جوف له , وذلك يتضمن نفي النهاية ونفي الحد والجهة والجسم والجوهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word teaches that knowledge requires both negation and affirmation, distinguishing truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: فقررت هذه الكلمة وجوب المعرفة بالنفي والثبات ليميز بين الحق وبالطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five names or attributes undergird the surah, likened to five religious pillars and the five words that make ten in Ayat al-Kursi: inward faith, worship, exclusive devotion, dependence, and recognition of need.
rows.anchor: ففيها من الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى , التي أسس عليها بنيانها , وانبنت عليها أركانها , خمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word count of fifteen alludes to the fifteenth year of prophethood and Badr, where God's aid made the surah's proof of unmatched divinity evident by witnessed experience.
rows.anchor: وكونها خمسة عشرة كلمة إشارة إلى أنهم في السنة الخامسة عشرة من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting the obligatory hidden pronoun in qul raises the count to sixteen, alluding to the sixteenth prophetic year and Uhud, when God's hidden name al-Batin was manifest through calamity.
rows.anchor: وإذا ضممت إليها الضمير الواجب الاستتار في { قل } كانت ست عشرة إشارة إلى أنه في السنة السادسة عشرة من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen pronoun alludes to Uhud's seventy fallen Muslims, including Hamza; after early victory, the later reversals reveal God's hidden support and the Prophet's steadfastness.
rows.anchor: من قتل سبعين من الصحابه رضي الله تعالى عنهم منهم حمزة بن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Uhud, only a small group remained with the Prophet against roughly three thousand foes, showing that God alone is the helper even when victory appears to turn against believers.
rows.anchor: فأخلى الله تعالى نصره لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها باسمه الباطن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was not aided at any other battle as he was at Uhud.
rows.anchor: وقد قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما نصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في موطن من المواطن ما نصر في غزوة أحد

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان ابن حرب
rows.claim: On accepting Islam at the conquest, Abu Sufyan tells the Prophet that he prevailed whenever they fought and infers that no other deity could have helped against him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سفيان ابن حرب يوم إسلامه في عام الفتح للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما قاتلتك من مرة إلا ظهرت علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's eighteen-letter count points to the fifth year after Hijra: at the Trench and against Banu Qurayza, God routed ten thousand attackers unseen and humbled the clans.
rows.anchor: فكانت الكلمات بذلك ثماني عشرة , كان إشارة إلى أن في السنة الثامنة عشرة من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the four basmala words to fifteen yields nineteen, alluding to Hudaybiyya in year six, which God called a victory and made the cause of later conquest.
rows.anchor: كلمات البسملة الأربع لتكون تسع عشرة فنوازي سنة ست من الهجرة , وذلك سنة عمرة الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the obligatory concealed pronoun gives twenty, corresponding to the following year's Umrat al-Qada, where tawhid appeared among the polytheists yet remained partly hidden.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها الضمير المستتر كانت عشرين , فوازت سنه سبع التي كانت فيها عمرة القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding two optional hidden pronouns gives twenty-two, corresponding to year nine: delegations, mass conversion, Abu Bakr's pilgrimage, and removal of polytheist rites from the sanctuary, though some concealment remained.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها الضميرين المستترين الجائزي البروز كات اثنتين وعشرين موازية لسنة تسع سنة الوفود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divinity entails oneness, but oneness alone does not entail divinity; the author therefore stresses the absolute unity expressed by aḥad.
rows.anchor: فالإلهية من حيث هي تقتضي الوحدة , والوحدة لا تقتضي الإلهية

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Divinity entails oneness but oneness alone does not entail divinity; aḥad conveys the utmost possible unity, beyond wahid's gradable applications, as Ibn Sina explains.
rows.anchor: والواحد - قال ابن سينا - مقول على ما تحته من التشكيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aḥad excludes every kind of plurality: genus and species, rational matter and form, potential or actual bodily parts, organs, shape, color, and any likeness that would make identity depend on parts.
rows.anchor: والأحد جامع لذلك دال عل الواحدية من جميع الوجوه , وأنه لا كثرة هناك أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No description reaches even a small portion of divine majesty; the highest human descriptions remain below what God disclosed in revelation.
rows.anchor: ولا يبلغ أدنى ما استأثره من الجلال والعظمة والبهجة أقصى نعوت الناعتين

rows.speaker: الأقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Iqlaishi records disagreement: some treat aḥad and wahid as synonyms; others derive one from the other through altered letters, while some regard aḥad as independent.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو العباس الاقليشي في شرح الأسماء الحسنى , فمن أهل اللسان من ساوى بينهما جعلها مترادفين , ومنهم من قال : أصل ( أحد ) واحد

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي والحرالي
rows.claim: The author draws on al-Razi and al-Harali to define wahid as having no plurality and aḥad as having no second or counterpart.
rows.anchor: منها شرح الفخر الرازي والفخر الحرالي وغيرهما - قالوا : الواحد الذي لا كثرة فيه بوجه

rows.speaker: الأقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Iqlaishi says true unity belongs only to what is not composite; calling a person or coin one is figurative, while God alone combines unity with majesty.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو العباس الاقليشي في شرح الأسماء الحسنى : هذه حقيقة الوحدة عند المحققين

rows.speaker: الأقليشي
rows.claim: A unique individual such as the Throne, Footstool, sun, or moon could still have a conceivable counterpart, so its individuality is not absolute divine oneness.
rows.anchor: وكل ما نوعيته في شخصيته كالعرش والكرسي والشمس والقمر يصح أن يقدر لها نظائر

rows.speaker: الأقليشي
rows.claim: A third sense is God's independent action and creation without dependence; unlike the preceding sense, it excludes a helper or minister, while the first excludes a second deity.
rows.anchor: ولها معنى ثالث وهو التوحيد بالفعل والإيجاد , فيفعل كل ما يريد من غير توقف على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound reason and decisive revelation establish one creator who is indivisible, without counterpart, independently creating, making, and governing; all people should invoke Him and His final messenger addressed all.
rows.anchor: قضى بهذا شاهد القعل المعصوم من ظلمة الهوى وكثافة الطبع , وورد به قواطع النقل ونواطق السمع

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali distinguishes indivisibility from having no counterpart: God cannot be divided or duplicated, while a sun is indivisible in one sense yet another could be imagined.
rows.anchor: وقال حجة الإسلام أبو حامد الغزالي في ىخر شرحه للأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: A human is called unique only relative to one excellence and peers; absolute uniqueness belongs only to God, who alone cannot be joined by another in existence.
rows.anchor: والعبد إنما يكون واحدا إذا لم يكن له في أبناء جنسه نظير في خصلة من خصال الخير

rows.speaker: الشهرستاني
rows.claim: Al-Shahrastani describes debate over whether the one begins number or stands outside it, distinguishing the unit repeated to make numbers from their causal source.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في الواحد أهو من العدم أم مبدأ العدد وليس داخلا في العدد

rows.speaker: الشهرستاني
rows.claim: Wahid can also describe every existing thing as one in its genus, species, or individual instance, unlike God's absolute oneness.
rows.anchor: وقد يلازم الواحدية جميع الأعداد لا على أن العدد يتركب بها بل وكل موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The numerical allusion culminates in year nine's mass conversions and cleansing of the sanctuary, then year ten's Farewell Pilgrimage, when no polytheist performed pilgrimage and Satan despaired of worship in Arabia.
rows.anchor: وفي العدد أنه لا كفوء له ولكن كان ذلك بوجه خفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah and basmala have sixty-six written and pronounced letters, matching Allah's name numerically and alluding to the unmatched sincerity of Muhammad and Abu Bakr and Islam's triumph over empires.
rows.anchor: أن حروفها مع البسملة النظر إليها من حيث اللفظ وكذا من حيث الرسم ستة وستون حرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifty spoken letters correspond to Ayat al-Kursi except the silent written alif in kufuwan; its hidden-yet-written letter figures God's hidden essence known through names and witnessed acts.
rows.anchor: وذلك خمسون حرفا إلا واحدا هو ألف { كفوا } الذي هو مرسوم غير ملفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing guidance of al-Fatiha and al-Baqara leads from the travelers' first station to the perfected monotheism and sincerity of al-Ikhlas, after which seekers devote themselves wholly to God.
rows.anchor: وختم بتقرير أمر التوحيد على وجه لا يتصور أن يكون أكمل منه وتقرير الإخلاص فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unattributed poetry likens the completed journey to a traveler settling after return, illustrating the repose that follows devotion.
rows.anchor: وألقت عصاها واطمأن بها النوى … كما قر عينا بلإياب المسافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq's purpose is refuge from the evils emerging from creation, inward and outward; its name makes that purpose evident.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاعتصام من شركل ما انفلق عنه الخلق الظاهر والباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's epithets portray God as possessing all power, gathering every perfection, and completing His gifts to those He loves with safety.
rows.anchor: { بسم الله } الذي له جميع الحول { الرحمن } الذي استجمع كمال الطول { الرحيم } الذي أتم على أهل وداده جميع النول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran opens with guidance and ends al-Ikhlas with unsurpassable monotheism and sincerity, completing religion and the travelers' course before the refuge surahs.
rows.anchor: وختم الإخلاص المقررة لذلك بأنه تعالى لا كفوء له ، فتوفرت الدواعي على الانقطاع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek refuge in the Lord accords with worship and seeking help; it protects against outward and inward harms from all creatures, including human and jinn satans.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتعوذ برب هذا الدين , موافقة لإياك نعبد وإياك نستعين , من شر ما يقدح فيه بضرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The progression begins with evils shared by visible and hidden realms, then names harms focused inward, whose correction also repairs the outward; it encourages recurring to the Quran's opening.
rows.anchor: ثم اتبع بما يعم القبيلين ويخص الباطن الذي يستلزم صلاحه صلاح الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qul teaches every creature to turn first to its overpowering Lord in adversity, correcting reliance into trust and acceptance rather than self-reliant planning that deepens regret.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كلهم مربوبون مقهورون لا نجاة لهم في شيء من الضرر إلا بعصمته سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿudhu means seeking protection, refuge, resort, and defense; the Lord's nurturing role especially fits the act of protection.
rows.anchor: { أعوذ } أي أستجير وألتجئ وأعتصم وأحترز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq is whatever God brings forth by splitting the darkness of nonexistence: springs split earth, rain clouds, plants soil, children wombs, and dawn night, bringing calm and joy.
rows.anchor: { برب الفلق * } أي الذي يربيه وينشئ منه ما يريد , وهو الشيء المفلق بإيجاده ظلمة العدم

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malwi expands al-Falaq to encompass all created beings, supporting the broad sense beyond dawn alone.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : والفلق - بالسكون والأنس والسرور إلى غير ذلك من سائر المخلوقات , الكائنات جميعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conventionally al-falaq is dawn, a visible change foreshadowing resurrection, the greatest splitting of annihilation's darkness; resurrection is no harder than initial creation, so God can protect from every fear.
rows.anchor: لأنه ظاهر في تغير الحال ومحاطاة يوم القيامة الذي هو أعظم فلق يشق ظلمة الفنا والهلاك بالبعث والإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The realm of command is wholly good, so evil is confined to created things; the request covers every creature except God and His attributes, whether rationally chosen, animal, or natural harm.
rows.anchor: وكان عالم الأمر خيرا كله , فكان الشر منحصرا في عالم الخلق خاصة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr notes that the connection between al-Falaq and al-Ikhlas was already indicated in the discussion of their coherence.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : قد أشير , أي في الكلام على ارتباط الإخلاص - إلى وجه ارتباطها آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specific evils follow the general category because they are especially harmful: darkness is corruption's root, while night, sorcery, and envy strike secretly and unexpectedly.
rows.anchor: وكان شر الأشياء الظلام , لإإنه أصل كل فساد , وكانت شرارته مع ذلك وشرارة السحر والحسد خفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ghasq ranges over darkness and flowing; it can mean early night, a dark or tearful eye, flowing milk, the moon, or setting Pleiades, whose setting was linked to epidemics and illness.
rows.anchor: وكانت مادة ( غسق ) تدور على الظلام والانصباب , فالغسق - محركة : ظلمة أول الليل

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon cited by the author links the setting of the Pleiades with many plagues and illnesses.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس : لكثرة الطواعين والأسقام عند سقوطها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other authorities are reported to apply ghasq to the male organ when erect, which can lead to ignorance through lust.
rows.anchor: والذكر - إذا قام , كما قاله جماعة وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse seeks refuge from darkness or cold that pours in and settles, whether literal or figurative; the moon can cause harmful bodily moisture and desire brings corrupt whispers, while the indefinite noun shows not every occurrence is evil.
rows.anchor: أي مظلم بارد منصب ظلامه وبرده سواء كان أصلا في الظلام حسيا أو معنويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqaba describes darkness entering forcefully and settling like dense matter in a rock cavity; harm grows once established, so it is easier to treat beforehand.
rows.anchor: وكان الظلام لا يشتد أذاه إلا إذا استقر وثبت , قال معبرا بأدة التحقق : { إذا وقب * } أي اعتكر ظلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes a hadith interpreting sunset as Maghrib time and a report from Abu Yaʿla that the Prophet told Aisha to seek refuge from the dark moon.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث ( لما رأى الشمس قد وقبت قال : هذا حين حلها ) يعني صلاة المغرب , وفيه عند أبي يعلى أنه قال لعائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن القمر : ( تعوذي بالله من شر هذا الغاسق إذا وقب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters identify the ghasq as night because harms multiply then and are harder to repel; waqaba primarily means entering a cavity, though some make fullness the root of ghasq.
rows.anchor: وأكثر الأقوال أنه الليل , خص بالاستعاذة لأن المضار فيه تكثر ويعسر دفعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sorcery is the most deeply settled darkness: it can separate spouses or family members, waste bodies, and kill, so it follows the discussion of night.
rows.anchor: ولما كان السحر أعظم ما يكون من ظلام الشر المستحكم في العروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's being bewitched does not contradict God's promise to protect him, because opponents meant that he was mad and that his speech was confused and false.
rows.anchor: ولا يوجب ذلك صدق الكفرة في وصفه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه مسحور , فإنهم ما أرادوا إلا الجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy, the wish that another lose a blessing, is a leading motive for sorcery and other harm; the author quotes unattributed poetry on the impossibility of appeasing an envier.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أعظم حامل على السحر وغيره من أذى الناس الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun is indefinite because not every envious person is blameworthy; Satan is the greatest envier, seeking to remove worship's blessings through heedlessness.
rows.anchor: ونكره لأنه ليس كل حاسد مذموما , وأعظم الحسدة الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy harms others only when expressed in action, such as the evil eye; otherwise only the envier suffers grief, and the verse intimates asking for blessings worth envying.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الضار من الحسد إنما هو ما أظهر وعمل بمقتضاه بالإصابة بالعين أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says persistent envy usually manifests unless God protects a person, and traces sorcery's deadly reach and even shirk to envy.
rows.anchor: ولعله عبر بأداة التحقيق إشعارا بأن من كلان ثابت الحسد متمكنا من الاتصاف به بما أشعر به التعبير بالوصف تحقق منه إظهاره

rows.speaker: الزبير بن العوام
rows.claim: Ahmad and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi report from al-Zubayr that envy and hatred are the illness of earlier nations, and hatred shaves religion rather than hair; reports from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud are also noted.
rows.anchor: عن الزبير بن العوام رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( دب إليكم داء الأمم قبلكم : الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's ending returns to its beginning: protection lets the heart's dawn split ignorance's darkness and shine with wisdom and spiritual insight.
rows.anchor: فعلم بهذا رجوع آخر السورة على أولها , وانعطاف مفصلها على موصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protection is attained through wholehearted following and avoidance of innovation, as the cited verse promises love for those who follow the Messenger.
rows.anchor: فينقطع التعلق عما سوى الله بمحض الاتباع والبعد عن الابتداع بمقتضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek refuge refutes Jabrism: if people were moved without choice like stones, commands would have no purpose; it also rejects the Qadari claim that people create their own acts.
rows.anchor: وقد بطل بالأمر بالاستعاذة قول الجبرية : إنا كالآلة لا فعل لنا أصلا ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surahs reject philosophers' view that cause and effect operate without divine connection: if causes necessarily produced effects, seeking refuge could not prevent harm.
rows.anchor: وقول الفلاسفة : إنه - إذا وجد السبب والمسبب حصل التأثير من غير احتياج إلى ربط إلهي كالنار والحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ashari Sunni view is that an effect occurs only when God creates it: when He allows the cause to proceed it follows, and otherwise it does not.
rows.anchor: وثبت قول الأشاعرة أهل السنة والجماعة أنه إذا وجد السبب والمسبب توقف وجود الأثر على إيجاد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two refuge surahs teach that many afflictions exist but God can repel them, sustaining both fear and hope, the core of worship.
rows.anchor: والسورتان معلمتان بأن البلايا كثيرة وهو قادر على دفعها , فهما حاملتان على الخوف والرجاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from exegetes, and al-Baghawi from Ibn Abbas and Aisha, that a Jewish servant was coaxed into giving Jews the Prophet's hair clippings and comb teeth; Labid ibn al-Aʿsam used them to bewitch him.
rows.anchor: أن غلاما من اليهود كان يخدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدبت إليه اليهود فلم يزالوا به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits from Ibn Abbas and Aisha the account of a Jewish servant whose hair clippings and comb teeth were used by Labid to bewitch the Prophet; the report says the Prophet became ill.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعائشة رضي الله عنهم أن غلاما من اليهود كان يخدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In Aisha's account, the Prophet said God had revealed his illness and sent Ali, al-Zubayr, and Ammar to investigate; they drew the well and found the spell.
rows.anchor: وقال لعائشة رضي الله عنها : ( يا عائشة ! أما شعرت أن الله أخبرني بدائي ! ثم بعث عليا والزبير وعمار بن ياسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two refuge surahs comprise eleven verses—five in al-Falaq and six in al-Nas—and each recited verse loosened one knot until the Prophet recovered fully.
rows.anchor: وهما إحدى عشرة آية : الفلق خمس والناس ست , فجعل كلما قرأ آية انحلت عقدة

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel recites a healing prayer seeking God's protection from all harm, envy, and the evil eye, and affirms that God heals.
rows.anchor: وجعل جبرائيل عليه الصلاة والسلام يقول : ( بسم الله أرقيك من كل شيء يؤذيك ومن حاسد وعين والله يشفيك )
